text.p: Swedish state-controlled bank Nordbanken said on Friday profitability targets would remain unchanged but net commission income should be at least 25 percent of net interest income.
In addition, it expected loan losses to rise slightly from current historical lows of around 0.14 percent of total lending.
The bank targets a 15 percent return on equity, but has posted figures of more than 20 percent since it was listed on the Stockholm Stock Exchange in 1995.
Analysts have called it Sweden's most profitable bank, and on Thursday it reported a 26 percent return on equity for the first half of 1997.

"Obviously we consider our targets but it is most important that we have a profitability target that relates to what other listed companies achieve," Nordbanken chief executive Hans Dalborg told Reuters in an interview.
Dalborg set a benchmark for net commission income should of 25 percent or more of net interest income.
"Net commission income should rise in relation to net interest income. With a larger net interest income we want to reach 25 percent or more if possible," he said.
In the first six months of the year, net commission income amounted to 25 percent of net interest income, up from 19 percent in the year-earlier period.
Dalborg said asset management is an important part of banking operations.
"We want to be larger on asset management. On June 30 we had 108 billion crowns under management... That figure is larger today," he said, adding that share trading was also performing well.
Dalborg expected loan losses to rise in coming quarters from their current low level.
In the first six months of the year, Nordbanken's loan losses fell to 194 million crowns from 260 million for a loan loss ratio of 0.14 percent compared with 0.27 percent for the full year 1996.
Dalborg has said in the past the bank's normalised loan loss ratio should be around 0.5 percent.
Nordbanken posted a 21 percent fall in six-month operating profit to 3.02 billion crowns.
